text: Continuous Integration, or CI, is a common practice in modern software development. When developers write new code, they regularly add it to a shared project. A CI system then automatically starts an automated build to check that the code works correctly. As part of this process, it also runs tests to make sure nothing is broken. This helps teams catch issues early, before they become big problems. CI pipelines often include several steps, such as building, testing, and preparing the software for release. By using CI, teams can work faster, reduce mistakes, and deliver better software.
